title: Portal Architecture
description: A continuously maintained, source-backed model of Portal's runtime and code architecture.

components.label: App shell
components.description: Platform entry points, navigation, settings, onboarding, and shared application chrome.

components.label: Chat
components.description: Conversation presentation, composition, streaming output, attachments, and model selection.

components.label: Operations
components.description: Sessions, cron, activity, skills, learning, mission-control, and the read-only harness file browser.

components.label: Wiki
components.description: Wiki browsing, editing, graph exploration, events, and timeline presentation.

components.label: Artifacts
components.description: Living artifact presentation, structured blocks, exports, and typed action surfaces.

components.label: Thought graph
components.description: Agent execution graph, session canvas, delegation, and reasoning visualization.

components.label: Chat state
components.description: Conversation lifecycle, backend-normalized events, persona state, and capability-aware orchestration.

components.label: Operations state
components.description: Session, cron, activity, feed, skill, settings, gateway-lifecycle, learning, and file-browser state machines.

components.label: Wiki state
components.description: Wiki graph and timeline loading, stale-result rejection, filtering, and selection state.

components.label: Backend contract
components.description: Chat backend protocol and event normalization seam for the harness gateway.

components.label: Harness services
components.description: Harness WebSocket JSON-RPC transport, cron polling, and push registration.

components.label: Artifact intents
components.description: Declared-intent contract for living artifacts: inert artifact-authored declarations, the nonce-gated bridge out of untrusted artifact content, revision-pinned dispatch, maintainer references, and the native-only session click-through seam.

components.label: Wiki source contract
components.description: Capability markers for knowledge sources: which source records an edit history, and which can report the ingestion events behind a page. Wiki surfaces gate their affordances on conformance rather than on backend identity.

components.label: Local services
components.description: Persistence, export, media, notifications, caching, reasoning, and device-local support services.

components.label: Domain models
components.description: Value types and wire/domain models shared across user experiences and service adapters.

components.label: Shared UI
components.description: Reusable presentation primitives that are not owned by a single product surface.

components.label: Utilities
components.description: Platform compatibility, parsing, rendering memoization, diagnostics, and pure layout helpers.

components.label: Harness gateway
components.description: Ethen-managed WebSocket JSON-RPC agent gateway and full runtime surface.

components.label: Device services
components.description: Keychain, notifications, files, media, and platform frameworks on macOS and iOS.

specified_edges.description: The application shell presents the conversation experience.
Chat views render and act through conversation state.
Operational surfaces render dedicated observable state.
A wiki resource selected in the runtime graph resolves its wiki path through the shared Graphs surface and opens that entry in the wiki reader.
Wiki views use graph and timeline view models.

Wiki surfaces test the source for capability conformance to decide what to offer: the changeset drawer requires an edit history, the events plot and feed require an ingestion log. A missing affordance means the backend has nothing to show.
The gateway serves the wiki graph, pages, changeset history and an event log whose entries carry the changesets they caused.
Conversation orchestration consumes the AgentBackend interface.
GatewayClient implements the AgentBackend protocol for the harness.
GatewayClient connects to the harness WebSocket JSON-RPC gateway.
Local services integrate with platform persistence, files, media, and notifications.
Artifact blocks render typed artifact and message models.

Artifact surfaces — including the generated 3D world hosted in its own window — render declared actions and dispatch clicks through the intent contract rather than acting on artifact content directly.
An intent click is dispatched as artifact.action.invoke/confirm against the pinned revision; the gateway resolves the registered handler from the binding ID.
Declared maintainer references resolve against cron state, so the product can distinguish an artifact a job actively tends from one that is merely mutable.
When an intent runs as a contained agent session, native code posts the session switch; the untrusted artifact page is never handed a session ID or navigation capability.

external_systems.label: Harness gateway
external_systems.description: The Hermes fork's gateway: every chat, session, wiki, skills, cron, learning, and artifact RPC crosses this boundary.

external_systems.label: Cloudflare Access
external_systems.protocol: CF_Authorization cookie on the gateway origin
external_systems.description: Zero-trust front door in front of a remotely hosted gateway; the client carries the Access cookie on WebSocket and HTTP requests.

external_systems.label: Apple MLX
external_systems.description: On-device language-model inference on Apple silicon for local chat, reasoning summaries, and skill summaries.

external_systems.label: Hugging Face Hub
external_systems.protocol: HTTPS model downloads through the MLX model factory
external_systems.description: Source of on-device model weights (mlx-community repositories); downloaded into the local model inventory.

external_systems.label: Apple Push Notification service
external_systems.protocol: Remote-notification registration; device token forwarded to the gateway
external_systems.description: Delivers gateway push notifications to the device when the app is not connected.

external_systems.label: User Notifications
external_systems.description: Local notification presentation, authorization, and notification-tap routing back into the app.

external_systems.label: Keychain
external_systems.description: Secure storage for gateway API keys, OAuth tokens, and Access cookies.

external_systems.label: Application Support files
external_systems.description: Per-user persistence for sessions, artifacts, skills, curricula, run history, and caches.

external_systems.label: UserDefaults
external_systems.description: Preferences, small state flags, and migration markers.

external_systems.label: X API
external_systems.protocol: HTTPS REST v2 with OAuth 2.0 PKCE
external_systems.description: Reads posts for the feed surface; authenticated per user through the X OAuth flow.

external_systems.label: WebKit
external_systems.protocol: WKWebView with an isolated content world
external_systems.description: Renders HTML artifacts and rich content; the only bridge from untrusted markup to native intents.

external_systems.label: SceneKit
external_systems.description: 3D layout of the wiki knowledge graph.

external_systems.label: On-device speech
external_systems.protocol: AVSpeechSynthesizer and FluidAudio / PocketTTS neural voices
external_systems.description: Speaks assistant replies locally; no audio leaves the device.

external_groups.label: Platform storage
external_groups.description: Everything the app persists on the device: the Application Support tree of JSON documents and directories, the UserDefaults keys, and the Keychain items. Each store is drawn writing the artifacts its source names.

external_groups.label: On-device inference
external_groups.description: Model loading and inference that never leaves the device: the MLX runtime for local language models and the neural speech engines. Both are in-process frameworks the engines run on.

ci._comment: The CI gates plane. Workflow structure (jobs, needs, artifacts, triggers) is read from .github/workflows; this block declares what the files cannot say: which family each workflow belongs to and what each ratchet measures. The compiler fails on a workflow with no family, a declared workflow with no file, a ratchet naming an unknown job, or a posture job that nothing declares.

tests.label: Tests
tests.question: Does it work? Each job runs and passes or fails on behavior.

ratchet.label: Ratchet
ratchet.question: Did a tracked metric get worse? Each job compares the tree against a committed baseline.

build.label: Build
build.question: Do the macOS and iOS apps build from the generated project, and does the offline UI smoke test pass?

architecture-pages.label: Pages
architecture-pages.question: Do the committed architecture model and site match what the compiler produces from this tree?

testflight.label: TestFlight
testflight.question: Can a signed iOS build be archived and uploaded after a merge or tag?

snapshot-record.label: Snapshot Record
snapshot-record.question: Re-record the View-snapshot goldens on the CI runner image the verify job uses.

architecture-maintenance.label: Architecture Maintenance
architecture-maintenance.question: Manual fallback that refreshes deterministic evidence and proposes semantic summaries as a pull request.

ratchets.title: Compiler warnings
ratchets.measures: Swift compiler warning sites, per category. The build is the source of truth; the baseline freezes pre-existing debt.
ratchets.patch: No warning on a line the PR added.

ratchets.title: Test coverage
ratchets.measures: Line coverage from swift test over the testable layers only (Models, Services, Utilities, ViewModels). Views are excluded: the unit suite cannot reach them.
ratchets.floor: Aggregate drops at most 0.5 pt vs base.
ratchets.patch: At least 80% of added executable lines covered; skipped under 10 lines.

ratchets.title: Skipped tests
ratchets.measures: Disabled, conditionally enabled, known-issue or XCTest-skipped tests: coverage that never runs.
ratchets.patch: No new skip on an added line.

ratchets.title: Dead code
ratchets.measures: Unused declarations from Periphery: unreferenced symbols, assign-only properties, redundant protocols, conformances and accessibility.
ratchets.patch: No finding on a line the PR added.

ratchets.title: Performance op-counts
ratchets.measures: Algorithmic operation counts (not time) for the hot pure layout paths over fixed fixtures under -DPERF_COUNTERS. Deterministic on any machine.
ratchets.floor: Every counter at most base; the ceiling is read from base via git show.

ratchets.title: Lint baseline
ratchets.measures: Pre-existing SwiftLint debt frozen per rule via swiftlint --baseline. The run itself is a Tests job; this ratchet is the lock on growing the baseline to silence a new violation.
ratchets.floor: A tracked rule's count may not grow; paydown or a new rule's initial freeze only.

ratchets.title: Secret ignore-list
ratchets.measures: Accepted gitleaks fingerprints: matches reviewed and judged not to be real secrets. The scan itself runs in the same job.
ratchets.floor: Count may not grow silently; each addition is justified in the PR.
